tests.prompt: Design an A2 print poster for a jazz night: 'Blue Hour Sessions', Friday 14 November, 21:00, Kanal Bar, tickets €12 at bluehour.club. Deliver a self-contained HTML/CSS poster and say how to export a print PDF.
tests.good: Exact copy spelled correctly; one focal element and clear headline > date/place > CTA hierarchy; at most 2 typefaces and a limited hex palette; A2 dimensions (420x594 mm) with 3 mm bleed and safe margins; contrast at least 4.5:1; export steps with @page size and embedded fonts.

tests.prompt: I need a launch graphic for my app 'Tidy' in Instagram 4:5, Instagram story, LinkedIn post and X header sizes. Generate the background with an image model and keep our exact tagline 'Clean inbox, clear head.'
tests.good: Correct sizes (1080x1350, 1080x1920, 1200x627, 1500x500); image prompt with no text and reserved empty space; tagline set as a separate text layer, not model-rendered; safe zones per format incl. story UI and header avatar; layout reflowed per ratio rather than scaled; consistency checks across the set.

tests.prompt: Create a logo for 'Harbor', a calm budgeting app. Give me three concepts as SVG and tell me how you tested them.
tests.good: Brief with adjectives and category clichés to avoid; three different mark types with one-sentence ideas; clean SVG (256 viewBox, paths not live text, exact angles, evenodd holes); tests at 16-32 px, one-colour and reversed, squint/mirror/rotation, distinctiveness; renders actually viewed; stops for the user's choice before building a full kit; trademark caveat.

tests.prompt: Make the graphics for a small community film festival, 'Short Nights', 6-8 March at the Old Mill Cinema: generated key art with no lettering, an A3 print poster, and an Instagram post and story. We have no copy yet, so write a headline and a two-line blurb too.
tests.good: States a short plan first: key art through image-creation (prompting-fundamentals.md: a text-free prompt with empty space reserved for type, a few takes compared), the headline and blurb through content-creation (conversion-copy.md: specific and short, no invented claims), then the set here (ai-image-posters.md, print-and-academic-posters.md, banners-social.md). Type goes on as a separate layer; A3 at 297x420 mm with 3 mm bleed; 1080x1350 and 1080x1920 with story safe zones, layouts reflowed rather than scaled; one frozen style block across the set; every word checked; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: I'm presenting a poster at a conference next month. It has to be A0 portrait and my supervisor wants an editable PowerPoint file so the co-authors can tweak it. The title, authors, affiliations, abstract, methods, results and references are in poster/content.md, and three figures are in poster/figures/ (fig1.png, fig2.png, fig3.png). Please build the poster and give me a PDF I can send to the printer too.
tests.good: Builds a real one-slide .pptx (python-pptx, not an image pasted on a slide) with the slide set to exactly 841 x 1189 mm and notes that PowerPoint's 56 in (142.24 cm) slide limit is fine for A0. Puts every text block in editable text boxes on a column grid with margins, using sizes readable from about 1.5 m (title around 85-120 pt, body at least 24-28 pt) and at most two common fonts, with the copy taken verbatim from content.md and no invented results, affiliations or citations. Places the three figures without distortion, works out each one's effective ppi at its printed size, and flags any figure below about 150 ppi instead of silently upscaling it; adds alt text to the figures. Exports a PDF (PowerPoint, or LibreOffice headless) and checks it with pdfinfo (page 2384 x 3370 pt) and pdffonts (all fonts embedded), plus contrast of at least 4.5:1. Renders a preview, looks at it at full size and at thumbnail size, and fixes overflowing or clipped text boxes. Delivers the .pptx and the PDF, and asks the user to confirm the conference's and printer's size, bleed and file rules rather than assuming them.

tools.name: Canva
tools.why: Canva reports 265M+ monthly users and 31M paying subscribers, and design round-ups (Guideflow, Toolradar) rank it with Adobe as the default fast route for social, flyers and brand templates; it has a Connect REST API (autofill, export) and an official MCP connector.

tools.name: Figma
tools.why: Round-ups (Guideflow, Toolradar, Storyflow) list Figma as the collaboration and brand-system standard next to Adobe and Canva; it has a REST API (files, image export, variables, comments) and an official remote MCP server with write access (use_figma).

tools.name: Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign (with Adobe Express and Firefly)
tools.why: Adobe Illustrator (2.21%) and Photoshop (1.64%) lead 6sense's graphic-design-software share and Creative Cloud tops the 2026 round-ups; Adobe shipped an official 'Adobe for Creativity' connector for Claude (Apr 2026, 50+ tools across Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, Express, Firefly) and Firefly Services has a Photoshop REST API (Enterprise contract).

tools.name: Playwright / headless Chrome (HTML to PNG and PDF)
tools.why: HTML/CSS rendered to PNG or print PDF is the default code route for exact-type posters, banners and social cards in this craft; Playwright is the leading driver (playwright-mcp 37.8k stars, playwright-cli 13.8k) and offers both page.screenshot and page.pdf.

tools.name: Gemini image models (Nano Banana)
tools.why: Google's Gemini image models (Nano Banana, Nano Banana 2, Nano Banana Pro) are a default image route with 'advanced text rendering', 0.5K to 4K output and many aspect ratios; Visme's 2026 AI design round-up and many Claude Code skills (400+ stars) are built around them.

tools.name: OpenAI GPT Image
tools.why: GPT Image is one of the two mainstream hosted image routes for posters and graphics (Visme and Rework 2026 round-ups); the Images API offers generations and masked edits, sizes at multiples of 16 up to 1536 px sides, and transparent PNG/WebP, though its docs admit text placement can still be imprecise.

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.why: Widely used for painterly and poster key art (V8.2 is the current default in 2026) but it has no official public API, so an agent can only write prompts and parameters (--ar, --sref, quoted text) for the user to run; docs site blocks automated fetch (403), existence confirmed via search results. Promoted to major: 2026 usage surveys put Midjourney first in user preference among image generators (26.8%, ahead of DALL-E/GPT Image) with about 19.8M users and ~$500M 2025 revenue, and describe it as where most creative pros start; market leaders are major even without an API.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.why: The text-in-image specialist (about 90-95% text accuracy per vendor and 2026 guides; 4.0 is open-weight with bounding-box layout control); has a REST API (generate, edit, remix, upscale, background removal) and an official OAuth MCP server.

tools.name: Recraft
tools.why: The main image model that outputs real SVG (models ending _vector) plus vectorize, background removal and custom styles, so it fits logos, icons and brand graphics; official remote MCP server with OAuth.

tools.name: Satori and @vercel/og (ImageResponse)
tools.why: The standard code route for dynamic Open Graph and social-card PNGs (Satori converts JSX/CSS to SVG, Resvg to PNG; 14k-star Satori, bundled in Next.js); limits are flexbox-only CSS, ttf/otf/woff fonts, 500 KB bundle, 1200x630 recommended.

tools.name: Inkscape (command line)
tools.why: The free, scriptable vector editor: `inkscape --export-type=png,pdf,eps` converts SVG to print and web formats and `--actions` batches edits; Guideflow and Toolradar-style lists include it as the open-source Illustrator alternative.

tools.name: Affinity (Designer, Photo, Publisher in one app)
tools.why: Canva made Affinity free in one app (v3.3 Sep 2026 adds a JavaScript Scripting Studio) and Guideflow and Toolradar list it as the cost-conscious Adobe alternative; an official Affinity AI Connector (MCP, beta) lets Claude write and run scripts in the app.

tools.name: CorelDRAW Graphics Suite
tools.why: 6sense's graphic-design-software share puts CorelDRAW at 2.08%, level with Illustrator (2.21%) and ahead of Photoshop (1.64%); PeerSpot gives it 7.1% mindshare (Feb 2026, rising) and 2026 poster-software round-ups name it the pick for print-ready vector posters. It is the standard in print shops and sign-makers (Windows-heavy). Automation is local only: JavaScript scripts run from Tools > Scripts (full object model via `host.ActiveDocument`, no UI), plus VBA/VSTA macros; no official MCP or cloud API.

tools.name: Microsoft PowerPoint (research and conference posters)
tools.why: University poster guides (Toronto, Xavier, Georgia State, Fourwaves) name PowerPoint the most commonly used software for academic and conference posters, ahead of Google Slides, Illustrator, Canva and LaTeX; research posters in PPTX are a named job in this craft's router. A poster is one slide at a custom size, capped at 56 in (142.24 cm) per side, so A0 (84.1 x 118.9 cm) fits but 48x96 in must be built at half scale. Agents build editable .pptx files with python-pptx; the presentations craft owns decks, not posters.

tools.name: Procreate
tools.why: The leading iPad illustration app (40M+ downloads, the best-selling paid iPad app) and, per 2026 illustration-industry surveys, the primary tool of about half of illustrators, so hand-drawn poster and cover art often arrives as Procreate exports (PSD, PNG, PDF). It has no API, scripting or AI features, so the agent's role is to set the canvas size and dpi for the poster and take the export into layout.
